Data was imbalanced (6% churn), so I used class weights and judged models on precision-recall AUC instead of accuracy. Final XGBoost model reached 0.71 PR-AUC and the retention team used the top-decile list to cut churn by 9% in one quarter. Delivered a reproducible pipeline and a short limitations report.

per_job_b.draft_raw:
Do you need an API that can keep up with 120 requests per second while still queuing 100k texts for sentiment scoring? A fast, reliable endpoint is critical for real‑time analytics and downstream decision making.

In 2025 I built a FastAPI sentiment service that handled 120 requests per second on a 2‑CPU machine, using a single Docker image and a Celery worker for background scoring of large batches.

First, I’ll add health checks, retry logic and a simple dashboard for monitoring job status. The next step is to review your current model and data pipeline so I can set up the worker and Dockerfile.

First, I’ll add health checks, retry logic and a simple dashboard for monitoring job status. The next step is to review your current model and data pipeline so I can set up the worker and Dockerfile.
answers: I would enqueue the 100k texts as a single Celery task, split them into manageable chunks inside the worker, and use retry logic to ensure all batches complete without blocking the API.

evidence.title: sentiment-api (GitHub README)
evidence.text: sentiment-api: a small service that serves a Hugging Face sentiment model behind FastAPI. One Dockerfile, health check, batch endpoint and load test results (120 requests per second on a 2-CPU box).

evidence.title: CV: Sara Malik
evidence.text: AI/ML engineer with 4 years of experience. Built classification models, NLP pipelines and retrieval-augmented chatbots for clients in telecom, legal and logistics. Comfortable taking a model from notebook to a FastAPI service in Docker on AWS. BSc Computer Science. Languages: Python, SQL. Tools: PyTorch, scikit-learn, Hugging Face, LangChain.

evidence.title: sentiment-api/worker.py
rag-eval-kit (GitHub README)
evidence.text: rag-eval-kit: scripts to measure search quality. Compares BM25, dense embeddings and hybrid fusion on your own labelled queries and reports Recall@k, MRR and nDCG. Used it to show a client that hybrid search fixed exact product-code queries.

evidence.title: Document Q&A chatbot for a law firm
evidence.text: Built a retrieval-augmented chatbot over 8,000 contract PDFs for a mid-size law firm. Chunked documents by clause, stored embeddings in Pinecone and served answers through FastAPI with citations to the source clause. Lawyers reported finding clauses in seconds instead of minutes. Added a 'no answer found' path so the bot never guessed.
